brief.headline: HBM4E samples ship, DRAM/NAND pricing decelerates into Q3 while hyperscaler capex hits $725B—memory pair trades deep red after Samsung EPS fails to impress
brief.summary: <cite index="6-8">SK Hynix shipped HBM4E samples to major customers on June 18, featuring 16Gbps pin speeds and 48GB 12-layer capacity</cite>, reinforcing its lead while <cite index="5-8">Samsung's Q3 2025 HBM share stood at 35% vs SK Hynix's 53%</cite>. <cite index="16-1">Conventional DRAM prices forecast to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND 10-15%, down sharply from Q1's 93-98% DRAM surge</cite>, as <cite index="12-9">AI inference and hyperscale demand keeps supply constrained while consumer markets weaken</cite>. <cite index="28-5,28-8">Hyperscaler 2026 capex now $725B, nearly double mid-2025 estimates of $365B</cite>, but <cite index="39-8,42-7">both stocks sold off 7-14% last week despite Samsung's record profit, with memory sector now in bear market down >20% from June highs</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="3-18">SK Hynix expected to achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite> vs Samsung playing catch-up on HBM3E qualification. <cite index="30-11">CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026</cite>, easing packaging bottleneck for both. Near-term relative: favor SK Hynix on HBM4E momentum and <cite index="3-12">62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025)</cite> vs Samsung's <cite index="48-7">heavy capex to narrow technology gap</cite> that may pressure near-term margins. Samsung re-rates only if HBM4 qualification materializes H2; until then SK Hynix owns the AI memory narrative despite valuation stretch.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-10">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ</cite>, <cite index="17-7,17-8">Q2 58-63% DRAM, 70-75% NAND</cite>, <cite index="16-1">Q3 forecast 13-18% DRAM, 10-15% NAND</cite>—deceleration clear. <cite index="4-42,4-43">HBM crowding out commodity DRAM capacity with 3-to-1 conversion ratio</cite>. <cite index="13-26,13-27">Buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes, NAND spot trading gone quiet—parabolic phase maturing, not peaked</cite>. Structural: AI server demand robust through 2027, but consumer destruction real.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-1,3-10">HBM3E expected to account for ~67% of total HBM shipments in 2026, HBM4 gradually increasing share</cite>. <cite index="8-11,8-14">Nvidia recently asked suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026; 12-layer HBM4 qualification ongoing, full commercial rollout early 2026</cite>. <cite index="10-1,10-5">Micron in high volume production of HBM4 36GB 12H, achieving >11 Gb/s pin speeds and >2.8 TB/s bandwidth</cite>. <cite index="3-9">NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra, Google TPU v7p/v7e, and Big Tech ASICs selecting HBM3E</cite>. Pricing: <cite index="1-9">analysts warn HBM prices could enter correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships HBM4E 12-layer samples, 16Gbps pin speed, 48GB capacity
news_pulse.implication: Reinforces technology lead; positions for next-gen Rubin/MI400 platforms; Samsung still qualifying HBM3E for Nvidia.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix shares plunge 7-14% despite Samsung record profit; memory sector in bear market
news_pulse.implication: Market pricing capex fatigue, AI monetization doubts; <cite index="42-11,42-12">semiconductor basket lost $1.5T market cap since June 25, Micron down $350B</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex hits $725B, up 77% YoY and double mid-2025 consensus of $365B
news_pulse.implication: Structural HBM/DRAM demand intact, but <cite index="29-3,29-4">$600B annual revenue gap between AI infra spend and ecosystem sales widening in 2026</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q3 price increase decelerates to 13-18% QoQ from Q1's 93-98%; NAND 10-15% vs Q2's 70-75%
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="12-4,12-5">Higher memory costs feeding through to retail, weighing on PC/smartphone demand; consumer affordability limit hit</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity reaching 120-140K wpm by end-2026, supply-demand gap narrows to 10% from 20%
news_pulse.implication: Packaging bottleneck easing; <cite index="33-6">Nvidia securing >60% of CoWoS for Blackwell/Rubin</cite>; benefits both Korean suppliers but more upside for Samsung if HBM4 qualifies.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64B) investment, M17 NAND fab construction starts 2027
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="39-12,39-13">80 trillion won to M17 NAND plant (ops 1H 2029), 20 trillion won to P&T7 advanced packaging; targeting HBM server/DRAM and enterprise SSD demand</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Commerce Sec Lutnick presses Samsung, SK Hynix to expand US memory production amid AI shortage
news_pulse.implication: Geopolitical pressure for onshoring; <cite index="46-1,46-2">Lutnick in discussions with both Korean suppliers to expand US capacity</cite>; potential policy risk/opportunity.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery; exploratory, no contracts signed
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="8-15,8-16">16-layer pulling forward generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full rollout; may be classified HBM4E</cite>; accelerates R&D burn.
